editionStated: The Uganda 'Infections and Infectious Diseases Prescribing' index page states: '2023 Uganda Clinical Guidelines'. The 'Other Common Clinical Conditions' section has a single item labelled 'UCG 2023' linking a PDF whose title page reads 'THE REPUBLIC OF UGANDA / MINISTRY OF HEALTH / Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023 / National Guidelines for Management of Common Health Conditions'. The site-wide footer says 'Clinical content in this toolkit is current as of March 31, 2026.' The About page names no edition. The individual HIV chapter page itself carries no edition statement. So: the site says it reproduces the 2023 edition, but ONLY the infection/antimicrobial sections are reproduced as web pages; the diabetes chapter is not among them.

findings.topic: SUMMARY: UCG diabetes chapter not obtained
findings.note: None of the requested clinical values (diagnostic criteria, prediabetes, screening, targets, treatment steps and level-of-care codes, cautions, monitoring, referral, DKA/HHS, hypoglycaemia threshold, diabetes in pregnancy, retinopathy) was read from the Uganda Clinical Guidelines, 2016 or 2023. What WAS read from UCG 2023: the table of contents (section numbers and pages), the Introduction's level-of-care sentence and its statement that the diabetes section was expanded, and the HIV chapter's diabetes-related lines.

findings.topic: UCG 2023 pagination differs between copies
findings.note: The nms.go.ug copy (file dated 2025/12) paginates the same sections 2-3 pages later than the DSD / prescribingcompanion copy (469 vs 471; 933 vs 936). There appear to be at least two printings of UCG 2023. Any page reference in the catalogue must name the copy. The fetch tool gave these as a list, not as quoted TOC lines.

findings.topic: UCG 2023 Introduction: diabetes section expanded in this edition
findings.quote: More attention has been paid to non-communicable chronic diseases; for example, stroke and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), and sections on diabetes, hypertension, asthma and mental conditions including diseases of elderly and dementia have been expanded.
findings.note: Reason not to assume the 2016 diabetes wording carries forward unchanged into 2023.

findings.topic: Level of care codes (UCG 2023 Introduction)
findings.quote: HC1-4 refers to health centres of different levels (with HC1 being the community level), H to general hospital, RR to regional referral hospital, and NR to national referral hospital.
findings.note: Identical sentence returned from the DSD copy.

findings.topic: UCG 2023 HIV chapter: dolutegravir contraindicated in known diabetics
findings.sectionHeading: 3.1 HIV Infection and AIDS: recommended first-line regimens (notes)
findings.quote: Contraindications for DTG (use DTG screening tool prior to DTG initiation) including: known diabetics, patients on anticonvulsants (carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital)
findings.note: This is UCG 2023 text as reproduced by prescribingcompanion.com. It conflicts with later evidence and with WHO practice; whether the 2022 HIV guideline keeps it could not be checked (its algorithm pages are beyond the readable part).

findings.topic: UCG 2023 HIV chapter: dolutegravir hyperglycaemia toxicity row
findings.sectionHeading: 3.1 HIV Infection and AIDS: ARV toxicity table, DTG row
findings.quote: DTG | 1. Hyperglycaemia 2. Insomnia 3. Hepatotoxicity 4. Hypersensitivity reactions | 1. Excessive drinking/eating, excessive urination ... | Do RBS to confirm hyperglycaemia then substitute with EFV
findings.note: Row returned cell by cell by the fetch tool; '...' marks the non-glucose symptom cells left out here. No glucose threshold is given in this row.

findings.topic: UCG 2023 HIV chapter: dolutegravir and metformin interaction
findings.sectionHeading: 3.1 HIV Infection and AIDS: important drug interactions
findings.quote: DTG increases metformin levels. May increase risk of hypoglycaemia and metabolic acidosis | Close follow-up (routine electrolytes, BUN and Creatinine, Random Blood Sugar tests) recommended

findings.topic: SECONDARY (not UCG text): which oral agents UCG 2023 names
findings.sectionHeading: Bonyani A et al. PLoS One 2025;20:e0326806, Discussion
findings.quote: the 2023 national clinical guideline lacks some of the OHAs listed in the EMHSLU 2023, mentioning only metformin, glibenclamide, and glimepiride
findings.note: Verbatim from a peer-reviewed paper ABOUT the UCG, not from the UCG. It gives names only: no order, no step, no level-of-care code. Note that glibenclamide is named in UCG 2023 but was deleted from EMHSLU 2023.

findings.topic: LEAD ONLY (third-party re-wording, edition unstated): hypoglycaemia threshold
findings.quote: Hypoglycaemia is a clinical condition due to reduced levels of blood sugar (glucose), with symptoms generally occurring when blood glucose is <3.0 mmol/L (55 mg/dl).
findings.note: NOT a UCG quote. A hobbyist question/answer dataset that names no source document or edition. Recorded only as a pointer to what UCG section 1.1.6 probably says; it must be confirmed against the guideline page before any rule uses it. The same dataset has rows on diabetes and DKA clinical features but no diagnostic thresholds.
